question.text: Ms. Neha Kulkarni (PM at Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund) runs a pair: LONG Stock P (Beta 1.2) and SHORT Stock Q (Beta 0.8). She invests INR 40 cr LONG in P. To make the pair Beta-neutral, what rupee SHORT in Q does she need?

explanation.text: The Logic: Beta-neutral requires Beta_long * Notional_long = Beta_short * Notional_short. 1.2 * 40 = 0.8 * Short => Short = 48 / 0.8 = INR 60 cr. Dollar-mismatch of 20 cr is intentional — lower-Beta short leg needs more rupee to offset the higher-Beta long. The Trap: Option A assumes dollar-neutral (ignores Betas). Option B inverts the ratio. Option D doubles incorrectly. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B tests similar Beta-hedging. VIII (Derivatives) uses the formula for index futures hedge quantity.
